questions.text: What is the primary purpose of the Model in the MVC architecture?
options: Direct the flow of control in the application
Manage the application's data and business logic
questions.warning: The notes call the Controller the part that "contains all the business logic". This question still wants the Model, since it's the only option about data.
questions.explanation: The Model interacts with the database and represents the application's data. Rendering the UI is the View's job; handling input and directing the flow is the Controller's.

questions.text: Which of the following is not one of the advantages of MVC listed in the notes?
options: A change in one part won't affect the other parts of the code
It helps a faster development process
It removes the need for a database
questions.explanation: The listed advantages are: organizing large projects, easier modification, changes in one part not affecting others, faster development, and helping Asynchronous Method Invocation. MVC still uses a database; the Model is the part that talks to it.

questions.text: Which of these are prerequisites for a Laravel development environment? Select all that apply.
options: Node, to compile the frontend assets
questions.explanation: The prerequisites are PHP >= 8.1, Composer, MySQL (or another supported DB), a web server or Laravel Sail, an IDE, and Node for compiling frontend assets. Java and Python aren't needed.

questions.text: ___ is a dependency manager for PHP.
questions.explanation: Composer installs and updates Laravel and brings in external dependencies, which it puts in the vendor folder.

questions.text: You open a terminal in /home/ana/sites and run the command below. Where does the new project end up?
options: Directly in /home/ana/sites, mixed in with whatever is already there
questions.explanation: create-project makes a subdirectory of the current directory named after the project, here blog. laravel/laravel is the package (skeleton) to build it from, not a folder.

questions.text: You run laravel new blog and the terminal says the laravel command isn't recognized. Which step was most likely skipped?
questions.explanation: The laravel new command comes from the Laravel Installer, which you first install globally with composer global require "laravel/installer". The other commands run inside a project that already exists.

questions.text: In Laravel, the primary configuration file is named ___.
questions.explanation: .env in the project root holds the environment-specific settings (app name, APP_KEY, database credentials). The files in config/ read their values from it. app.blade.php is a layout view, not configuration.

questions.text: Match each description to the directory that holds it.

pairs.term: Compiled Blade templates, logs and file-based sessions
index.php, the entry point for every request
Your Composer dependencies
Migrations, model factories and seeds
All of the configuration files
Pest or PHPUnit unit and feature tests

questions.explanation: The trap is the first one: the Blade source files live in resources/views, but the compiled versions go in storage, along with logs, file sessions and file caches. public holds index.php plus images, JS and CSS.

questions.text: The ___ directory contains the Blade views for your application.
questions.explanation: Views are stored in resources/views. Controllers live in app/Http/Controllers.

questions.text: The ___ directory holds the database migrations for your application.
questions.explanation: Migrations go in database/migrations. The database folder as a whole also holds model factories and seeds, so the full path is the answer.

questions.text: Where would you place your application's middleware?
questions.explanation: Middleware classes go in app/Http/Middleware/, next to app/Http/Controllers/. (Since Laravel 11 that folder isn't created until you make your first middleware with php artisan make:middleware, but that's still where it goes.)

questions.text: Which of the following occurs last in the request lifecycle?
questions.explanation: A request enters through public/index.php, service providers are registered, the router matches a route, middleware runs, the controller or closure runs, and finally a response is created and sent back. Response creation is the last step.

questions.text: Eloquent ORM: ORM means ___. (Spell it with the hyphen.)
questions.explanation: ORM stands for Object-Relational Mapping. Eloquent lets you write database queries in PHP syntax instead of SQL, with each table mapped to a model class.

questions.text: How can you define a route that accepts a parameter in Laravel?
questions.explanation: Route parameters go in curly braces in the path: /user/{id}. Query strings (?id=) aren't part of a route path, and :id is Express.js syntax, not Laravel's.

questions.text: What happens when someone visits /user with this route?
options: It shows User with nothing after it
It throws an error, because $name has no default value
questions.explanation: The ? makes /user match the route, so it's not a 404. But Laravel then calls the closure with no argument, and since $name has no default PHP throws an ArgumentCountError ("Too few arguments"). An optional parameter needs both the ? and a default, e.g. function ($name = 'Guest'). Verified by running the closure with no argument in PHP 8.2.

questions.text: Which URLs match this route? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: [A-Za-z]+ allows only upper- and lowercase letters, one or more of them. Digits and hyphens aren't in the class, so john123 and john-doe get a 404. Checked with preg_match in PHP.

questions.text: The route below is later changed from '/profile' to '/my-profile', but its name stays the same. What happens to the route('profile') calls spread across your views?
options: They now generate /my-profile, with nothing else to change
Each one has to be edited to route('my-profile')
They still generate /profile, which now returns 404
Laravel throws an error because the name no longer matches the path
questions.explanation: That is the point of named routes: route('profile') looks up the URL by name each time, so changing the path in one place updates every link and redirect.

questions.text: To create a route group that applies middleware to all routes within the group, which method should be used?
questions.warning: In real code the two go together: Route::middleware('auth')->group(function () { ... });. middleware() names the middleware, but group() is the method that creates the group, so that's the answer.
questions.explanation: group() wraps a set of routes so they share attributes such as middleware, a URL prefix or a name prefix. middleware(), prefix() and namespace() set those attributes; on their own they don't group anything.

questions.text: What does this fallback route send back?
options: The view resources/views/errors/404.blade.php, with no data, and HTTP status 404
The view errors.404, given the data array [404]
HTTP status 200, with errors.404 as the page title
questions.explanation: response()->view() takes the view name, the data array, and the status code. errors.404 uses dot notation for resources/views/errors/404.blade.php, [] passes no data, and 404 sets the status so the browser knows the page wasn't found.

questions.text: The Artisan command "php artisan ___" shows a list of all routes defined in your application.
questions.explanation: php artisan route:list prints every registered route with its method, URI, name and action.

questions.text: You ran php artisan route:cache on the production server, then added a new route, but it still returns 404. Fill in the command that clears the route cache: php artisan ___
questions.explanation: While routes are cached, Laravel serves the cached copy and ignores changes to web.php. php artisan route:clear removes the cache (run route:cache again afterwards if you want it cached in production).

questions.text: Match the following HTTP verbs.

pairs.term: Request a resource
Overwrite a resource.
Modify a resource

questions.explanation: GET requests a resource. PUT overwrites (replaces) the whole resource, while PATCH modifies part of it. POST creates a resource and DELETE removes it.

questions.text: Which directive is used to display data in a Blade view while escaping HTML?
questions.explanation: {{ }} runs the value through htmlspecialchars before printing it. {!! !!} prints it unescaped, and @{{ }} tells Blade to leave the braces alone (for JavaScript frameworks). @echo isn't a Blade directive.

questions.text: The route passes ['name' => '<b>Hi</b>'] to a view containing Hello, {{ $name }}. What does the visitor see?
options: Hello, <b>Hi</b>. (the tags shown as plain text)
An error, because echoes can't contain HTML
questions.explanation: {{ }} escapes the value, so <b> becomes <b> and the browser shows the tags as text instead of making the word bold. Checked with htmlspecialchars in PHP.

questions.text: A Blade view contains both comments below. Which ones can a visitor find with View Page Source?
questions.explanation: <!-- --> is a normal HTML comment, so it's sent to the browser and shows in the source. Blade comments {{-- --}} are removed when the template compiles and never reach the HTML.

questions.text: What does this output when $i is 2?
questions.explanation: @case(2) has no @break, so it falls through into @case(3), prints Third, and stops at that @break. Blade compiles @switch into a plain PHP switch; ran the equivalent PHP and got Second Third.

questions.text: What does this output when $records holds 3 items?
questions.context:
@if (count($records) >= 1)
    I have one record!
@elseif (count($records) > 1)
    I have multiple records!
@else
    I don't have any records!
@endif
options: I have one record! I have multiple records!
questions.explanation: Only the first true branch runs. 3 >= 1 is true, so the @elseif is never checked, even though it's also true. (The notes' version uses === 1, which avoids this.)

questions.text: This form updates a user. Why is it method="POST" instead of method="PUT"?
options: HTML forms can only send GET or POST, so Laravel reads the hidden _method field from the POST and treats it as PUT
Laravel rejects PUT requests that come from browsers
@method only works when CSRF protection is turned off
POST requests are faster than PUT requests
questions.explanation: HTML forms can't send PUT, PATCH or DELETE. @method('PUT') adds a hidden _method field, and Laravel uses it to send the POST to a Route::put route. @csrf is still needed.

questions.text: Fill in the edit form so it reaches the update route below.
questions.explanation:
1. POST: forms can only send GET or POST.
  2. csrf: every POST form needs @csrf for the hidden token.
  3. PUT: the route is Route::put, so the form spoofs PUT.

questions.text: To create a new controller, you can use the command ___.
questions.explanation: php artisan make:controller UserController creates app/Http/Controllers/UserController.php. There's no space after the colon and no parentheses.

questions.text: Which controller method is responsible for displaying a list of resources?
questions.explanation: index() lists the resources. show() displays a single one. all() is an Eloquent method (User::all()) you'd call inside index().

questions.text: Which of the following is not a default resourceful method in a controller?
questions.explanation: The seven resource methods are index, create, store, show, edit, update and destroy. submit() isn't one of them.

questions.text: Which method is used to handle the deletion of a resource in a resource controller?
questions.explanation: The controller method is destroy(). Inside it you call the model's delete() ($user->delete()), which is why delete() is the tempting wrong answer.

questions.text: Match each job to the resource controller method that does it.

pairs.term: Show the form for adding a new user
Validate and save the submitted new user
Show the form for changing an existing user
Validate and save the changes to an existing user
Display one user
List all users
Delete a user

questions.explanation: The form methods (create, edit) only show a form. The methods that receive it (store, update) validate and save.

questions.text: Which file does this line render?
questions.explanation: Dots in a view name mean folders, so users.index is resources/views/users/index.blade.php. compact('users') builds ['users' => $users], so the view gets $users.

questions.text: With the controller below, what happens when someone visits /user/999 and no user has that id?
questions.context:
public function show(string $id): View
{
    return view('user.profile', [
        'user' => User::findOrFail($id)
    ]);
}
options: The view renders with $user set to null
A 500 error saying the view is missing
Laravel creates a new user with id 999
questions.explanation: findOrFail throws a ModelNotFoundException when nothing matches, and Laravel turns that into a 404 response. Plain find() would return null instead.

questions.text: In a normal form submission, what happens when $request->validate([...]) fails?
options: A ValidationException is thrown, and Laravel redirects back with the errors and old input flashed to the session
validate() returns false and the method keeps running
The record is saved anyway and the errors are written to storage/logs
The user sees a 500 Internal Server Error page
questions.explanation: On failure an Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException is thrown. Laravel redirects the user back, flashes the errors and input to the session, and shares $errors with the views. The code after validate() never runs.

questions.text: Which of these correctly say that username is required and at most 50 characters? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Rules can be one string separated by | or an array of rules. The commas in required,max:50 don't separate rules, and rule parameters use a colon (max:50), not =.

questions.text: Which input passes this rule?
questions.explanation: digits_between:5,8 needs only digits, 5 to 8 of them, and both ends count. 1234 is too short, 123456789 is too long, and 12a45 has a letter.

questions.text: The password field uses the rule below. What else must the form send for it to pass?
options: A password_confirmation field with the same value
A password_2 field with the same value
Nothing; confirmed just checks the password isn't empty
questions.explanation: confirmed looks for a field named after the original plus _confirmation, so password needs password_confirmation with the same value.

questions.text: A user types abc into the age field. Which errors come back?
options: Only the numeric error, because bail stops checking age after the first failure
questions.explanation: Without bail Laravel would keep checking and report min:18 as well. With bail it stops at the first failed rule for that attribute, so only the numeric error is reported.

questions.text: The old password is secret123 and the user enters secret123 as the new one. What happens?
options: It passes, because the field isn't empty
It fails, because new_password must not equal old_password
It fails, because there's no new_password_confirmation field
It passes, because different only compares lengths
questions.explanation: different:old_password requires the value to differ from the old_password field. same is the opposite rule, and _confirmation fields belong to confirmed.

questions.text: Which input fails this rule?
questions.explanation: nullable allows an empty value, but a value that is given still has to pass the other rules. A 51-character string breaks max:50. Spaces are fine for string.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks to show the email field's first error message under the input.
questions.explanation: @error('email') runs its block only when email has errors, and inside it $message holds that field's message. $errors is the bag with every field's errors.

questions.text: The main database migration command is ___.
questions.explanation: php artisan migrate runs all pending migrations and creates or updates the tables. It's a command, so no () at the end.

questions.text: Running php artisan make:migration create_product_table creates the product table in the database right away.
questions.explanation: make:migration only writes the migration file into database/migrations. The table is created when you run php artisan migrate.

questions.text: A migration's up() method runs Schema::create('products', ...). What should its down() method do?
options: Nothing; down() is optional and Laravel undoes up() automatically
questions.explanation: down() must reverse what up() did so rollbacks work. up() created the table, so down() drops it.

questions.text: Match each migration command to what it does.

pairs.term: Run every pending migration
Roll back the most recent migrations (you can also name the connection)
Roll back every migration, not just the last batch
Roll back every migration, then run them all again

questions.explanation: rollback undoes the last batch only. reset undoes all of them and stops there. refresh does a reset and then migrates again, so you end up with freshly built tables.

questions.text: To create a new model, you can use the command "php artisan ___".
questions.explanation: php artisan make:model Product creates app/Models/Product.php. make alone isn't a command; it always needs a type after the colon.

questions.text: Without any extra settings, which table does a model named StudentRecord use?
questions.explanation: Models are singular PascalCase, and Laravel assumes the table is the plural in snake_case: StudentRecord uses student_records.

questions.text: The StudentRecord model has to use an existing table named tbl_students. What do you add to the model?
options: Nothing; Laravel finds the table automatically
questions.explanation: $table sets the model's table when it doesn't follow the naming convention. $fillable lists the columns that can be mass-assigned, and $model isn't a model property.

questions.text: The User model has protected $fillable = ['name', 'email'];. What happens with this call?
questions.explanation: $fillable lists which columns can be mass-assigned. By default Laravel silently drops anything not in it, which is how it stops a user from sneaking in is_admin.

questions.text: Going by the notes' description of $table->float('price', 8, 2);, what is the largest value price can hold?
questions.warning: Since Laravel 11, float() takes only one precision argument, so the 8-total, 2-decimal form now belongs to $table->decimal('price', 8, 2). Answer with the notes' meaning.
questions.explanation: 8 is the total number of digits and 2 of them come after the decimal point, so 6 are left before it: 999999.99.

questions.text: What does this line do in a migration for an orders table?
options: Adds a user_id column whose values must match an existing id in the users table
Creates the users table if it doesn't exist yet
questions.explanation: foreignId creates the column (an unsigned big integer, matching $table->id()), and constrained('users') adds a foreign key to users.id. The users table has to exist already.

questions.text: Fill in the migration so that id is an auto-incrementing primary key, no two students can share an email, is_active is true unless a value is given, and bio can be left empty.
questions.explanation:
1. id: $table->id() is the auto-incrementing big-integer primary key.
  2. unique: no two rows can share a value.
  3. default: ->default(true) fills it in when none is given.
  4. nullable: the column accepts NULL, so it can be left out.
